card.name: Qualifiers in monitoring and tapering instructions
card.fires_on: Small qualifying words that follow a stated schedule or instruction and open a caveat, such as "more frequently", "but with recognition", "as clinically indicated" and "a longer period may be appropriate". It appears in monitoring and discontinuation instructions.

modes.label: More often if needed
modes.description: Words like "frequently" or "as" that extend a monitoring schedule to a more frequent or as-needed one.
modes.example: then monthly thereafter, or more<< frequently>> following the occurrence of Grade 2 or

modes.label: Tapering caveat
modes.description: "but" and "with" after "as rapidly as is feasible", introducing a caution about stopping treatment.
modes.example: medication should be tapered, as rapidly as is feasible,<< but>> with recognition that abrupt discontinuation can be

modes.label: Longer period allowed
modes.description: The adjective after "may be" that allows a longer observation period.
modes.example: A longer period may be<< appropriate>> in patients with an increased risk of hypers
